blinding_guess.why: All nine SystemInterface members are declared with the override keyword and match the Humble-era signatures (read/write taking rclcpp::Time and rclcpp::Duration, CallbackReturn lifecycle callbacks), so no declaration-level mismatch is visible from the snapshot alone. The implementations have questionable behaviour (read() copies O_T_EE_d, a desired pose, into the 'ee_cartesian_velocity' state interfaces; on_init logs FATAL on wrong state-interface names but does not return ERROR; write() returns OK while the robot is in error; the multi-arm on_init recreates the executor on every arm), but whether any of these counts as the defect in question cannot be told without the paired side.

notes: Package defines two pluginlib classes deriving from hardware_interface::SystemInterface (franka_hardware/FrankaHardwareInterface and franka_hardware/FrankaMultiHardwareInterface, franka_hardware.xml); both declare all nine packet methods with textually identical declarations, so each declares entry is shared. All packet elements are C++ API symbols, not DDS entities: msg_type, units, QoS, rates and definition_id do not apply and are null. frame is 'none' for the lifecycle and mode-switch callbacks; for export_state_interfaces, export_command_interfaces, read and write the carried data are spatial (joint position/velocity/effort, a 16-element Cartesian pose from libfranka O_T_EE) but the code hard-codes no frame name, so frame is null. Joint interface prefixes come at run time from the URDF via info_.joints[i].name (e.g. franka_description panda_arm.ros2_control.xacro); on_init requires exactly 7 joints (7*robot_count for multi-arm) with 3 command and 3 state interfaces each, and reads hardware parameter robot_ip (robot_ip_<n>, ns_<n>, robot_count for multi-arm). exclusive lists the exported CommandInterface (prefix, interface name) argument pairs, which ros2_control lets only one controller claim at a time; the hardware itself also opens a franka::Robot connection to robot_ip (robot.cpp:36), whose exclusivity is a libfranka property not declared in this code, so it is not listed. The read/write call rate is set by the controller manager (update_rate: 1000 in franka_bringup/config/controllers.yaml, a different package), not by this package, so rate_hz is null. on_init overrides also call the base hardware_interface::SystemInterface::on_init(info) (src/franka_hardware_interface.cpp:171, src/franka_multi_hardware_interface.cpp:22). Besides the packet elements, the package offers services under nodes error_recovery_service_server and param_service_server (franka_msgs/srv/ErrorRecovery, SetJointStiffness, SetCartesianStiffness, SetTCPFrame, SetStiffnessFrame, SetForceTorqueCollisionBehavior, SetFullCollisionBehavior, SetLoad); these are outside the packet and not recorded as ports. manifest version is the placeholder 0.0.0 as written in package.xml.
